subject.title: [Tech Debt]: Config doctor does not remove retired environment variable references in profiles

question: Should doctor prune top-level config env entries after legacy profile/provider migrations, and what exact deletion boundary is safe?
rationale: The config `env` block is documented and schematized as a trusted credential source, so automation cannot safely infer that an unreferenced-looking variable is obsolete without maintainer policy on ownership markers and preservation.

options.title: Prune only owned retired refs
options.body: Add a conservative doctor cleanup that removes only env keys proven to be OpenClaw-generated or tied to a migrated retired reference, while preserving all other config env values.

options.title: Warn but do not delete
options.body: Have doctor report orphan candidates with manual guidance, avoiding credential deletion until a stronger ownership signal exists.

options.title: Generic unreferenced sweep
options.body: Delete any config env entry not referenced by current config/auth stores, accepting possible breakage for env-only provider or plugin setups.

recommendation.title: Prune only owned retired refs
recommendation.body: Add a conservative doctor cleanup that removes only env keys proven to be OpenClaw-generated or tied to a migrated retired reference, while preserving all other config env values.

likelyOwner.reason: This handle is the strongest current-history signal for the env/config, OpenAI provider unification, and auth-profile migration surfaces involved in the policy choice.
